title: Check yourself: choosing and using the java.time types

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An audit table records when each order was approved, in a LocalDateTime column filled with LocalDateTime.now() on servers whose JVMs ran in Europe/Amsterdam. The service moves to servers whose JVMs run in UTC, and a new report converts every stored value with atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).toInstant() to list approvals by the moment they happened. What does it show for the approvals stored before the move?

options.text: Each one at a moment later than it happened, since the stored value has no offset and the report supplies one for it
options.says: a LocalDateTime holds no zone or offset, so turning it back into a moment uses whatever zone the reader passes; Amsterdam's +01:00/+02:00 readings taken as UTC land one or two hours late

options.text: Each one at the moment it happened, since the stored value has no offset and the conversion supplies the one it was written with
options.says: the offset was dropped when the value became a LocalDateTime; the conversion uses the zone it is given, UTC, not Amsterdam's

options.text: An error for each one, since a value stored without an offset can't be converted to an Instant
options.says: only a conversion that supplies no zone, such as Instant.from(ldt), fails; atZone(...) gives the zone, so the conversion succeeds with whatever zone it is given

options.text: An error for each one, since the value was written under zone rules other than the ones the report runs with
options.says: a LocalDateTime carries no zone rules to compare; the conversion uses the zone it is given and succeeds

origin.section: Each Type Answers One Question, and Only Instant Is a Moment

questions.stem: A courier in Auckland (UTC+12 in June) records each delivery as an Instant. The daily summary runs on a server set to UTC and files each delivery under LocalDate.ofInstant(delivered, ZoneId.systemDefault()). A parcel is delivered at 08:00 on 10 June, Auckland time. Under which date does the summary file it?

options.text: 10 June, since the Instant carries the zone it was recorded in, and ofInstant uses that
options.says: an Instant has no date and no zone; the date comes from the zone passed to ofInstant

options.text: 10 June, since ofInstant dates the value in the zone where it was recorded
options.says: ofInstant uses the zone it is given, here the server's default, not the place of the event

options.text: 9 June, since ofInstant dates the value in the zone it is passed
options.says: 08:00 in Auckland is 20:00 UTC the day before, and ZoneId.systemDefault() is UTC on this server

options.text: 9 June, since the Instant is kept in UTC, and ofInstant uses that
options.says: ofInstant applies the zone argument, not a zone stored in the Instant; the answer is 9 June only because this server's default zone is UTC

origin.section: Between a Moment and a Date There Is Always a Zone

questions.stem: A hotel booking holds its check-out date as a LocalDate field returned by checkOut(). To let a guest leave a day early, the service runs `booking.checkOut().minusDays(1); repository.save(booking);`. A guest booked from 12 to 15 May. Which check-out date does the repository hold afterwards?

options.text: 15 May, since minusDays returns a new date and the code never stores it
options.says: java.time values are immutable: minusDays leaves the date it was called on unchanged and returns 14 May, which the code drops

options.text: 15 May, since save() writes the booking as it was loaded and skips changed fields
options.says: nothing changed: the booking's date is the same object as before, because minusDays never altered it

options.text: 14 May, since minusDays changes the date that the booking's field refers to
options.says: that is Calendar.add's behaviour; a LocalDate never changes after it is created

options.text: 14 May, since checkOut() hands out the field itself, so a change to it reaches the booking
options.says: handing out the field is safe precisely because a LocalDate can't be changed; minusDays returned a separate date

origin.section: Values Never Change: Keep What plusDays Returns

questions.stem: A shop in Singapore issues coupons valid until the end of 31 December, Singapore time. The coupon service checks `!LocalDate.now().isAfter(lastDay)`. The team wants a test that shows a coupon is refused at 00:00:30 on 1 January in Singapore (2026-12-31T16:00:30Z), and the test must give the same result on any day and on any machine. Which change makes that possible?

options.text: The service takes a Clock and reads LocalDate.now(clock); the test passes Clock.fixed(2026-12-31T16:00:30Z, ZoneId.of("Asia/Singapore"))
options.says: a Clock supplies both the instant and the zone that now(clock) reads, so a fixed clock in the shop's zone decides the date: 1 January, on any day and machine

options.text: The service takes a Clock and reads LocalDate.now(clock.withZone(ZoneOffset.UTC)); the test passes Clock.fixed(2026-12-31T16:00:30Z, ZoneId.of("Asia/Singapore"))
options.says: withZone(UTC) dates the fixed instant in UTC, where it is still 31 December, so the coupon is accepted

options.text: The service keeps LocalDate.now(); the test JVM runs with -Duser.timezone=Asia/Singapore
options.says: the default zone is only one of now()'s two inputs; the instant still comes from the system clock, so the result depends on the day the test runs

options.text: The service takes a ZoneId and reads LocalDate.now(zone); the test passes ZoneId.of("Asia/Singapore")
options.says: now(zone) still reads the system clock; only the zone is chosen, not the instant

origin.section: Code That Needs the Current Time Takes a Clock

concepts: Because the values are immutable and thread-safe, a constant can be shared across threads and a getter can return its field without a defensive copy.
A LocalDateTime holds no zone or offset, so it becomes a moment only with a zone supplied by the reader; Instant.from refuses it, and a wrong zone gives a wrong moment without an error.

java.time has one type per question: Instant for a moment, ZonedDateTime and OffsetDateTime for a wall-clock reading with a zone or offset, LocalDateTime/LocalDate/LocalTime for values with no place, ZoneId/ZoneOffset for the rules, Duration and Period for amounts.
